interactions.title: The Fox and Hunter answer prayers before dawn
lines: DM: But before we proceed, we go back to the night when the world turns and the night falls, and the stars begin to flicker over the sky. And the Fox and Hunter, the constellation, drift above the horizon, watching the sky dark and empty. 2,529th new moon that they have seen. Their attention, as always, is drawn to the borderlands west and north of their old homeland of Isingue, where the rangers guard the settled realms from the dangers of the Plaguelands.

DM: The prayers are numerous tonight. People pray for hope, healing, for escape to safety. To protect their loved ones, to survive the coming battle, to be brave in the face of their fear. There's little that one can do against this onslaught of prayers.

DM: On a hidden track, a captain at arms, Martin Strongbow, pauses in his nighttime gallop to tend his horse, offering a prayer for speed. The Fox breathes what life he can into the limbs of the man's horse. It stamps impatiently, eager for the race. The Hunter sees the path ahead, casting sight into the man's eyes to guide him in darkness. He'll ride far tonight, gathering troops to muster, protect the hidden life rescued from Isingue.

DM: The Hunter, as he does every night, spares a glance for this hidden magic, the blessing from the days of myth that the Rangers call the Heartroot. Frailty still clings to it, the wrongness of its shape here, away from home, apart from the contours and the flow and the path of the river that gave it birth. But as he does every night, the Hunter breathes life into the Heartroot, sustaining it in this unnatural space for another day, until it can be returned home.

DM: Many prayers come from the gathering at Three Wells. A familiar presence, a dear servant and ally, Cateline Malras, offers prayers of thanks for the aid that has arrived unexpectedly. Her prayers are the strongest, of course, and easiest to grasp, but they're just one of many of the prayers of thanks and hope that echo from Three Wells.

DM: As the night turns, the Fox and Hunter glance at the hobgoblins moving across the Plaguelands. The rippling echoes of Limbo still cling to them, the same strange contamination that has been growing the past two months. Worried, the gaze of the Fox and Hunter linger on these creatures as dawn breaks, and their movement slows to a halt as they begin to set camp for the day under a blanket of ash.
